category.name: Insider threat
category.description: Malicious, negligent or compromised insiders: departing staff, privileged misuse, fraud, sabotage and fraudulent workers, with HR and legal coordination.

playbooks.name: Departing employee suspected of taking company data
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee who has resigned or been given notice shows signs of collecting company data. Coordinates HR, Legal and Security on a proportionate, documented review.

preparation: Agree an HR-to-Security notification for resignations from high-risk roles within one business day
Have Legal approve a standard departure monitoring scope that respects local employee privacy law
Include return-of-property and data clauses in offboarding checklists
identification: Open a restricted-access case with need-to-know limited to HR, Legal and named investigators
Review the 30 days before notice for USB writes, personal email sends and cloud uploads
Check whether the employee is joining a competitor, using only HR-supplied information
Compare file access volume with the employee's own historic baseline
Document every search performed and its business justification for the privacy record
containment: Agree with HR whether to place the employee on garden leave and remove access early
Disable external sharing and USB write on the employee's account and device
Place the mailbox, OneDrive and device on legal hold before offboarding wipes them
eradication: Collect company devices at exit and image them before reassignment
Have Legal issue a letter requesting return or deletion of identified data
Revoke all SSO sessions, tokens and VPN certificates on the last day
recovery: Obtain a signed exit certification that no company data is retained
Brief the manager on accounts and projects that need transition handling
Close the case with a factual findings memo shared only with HR and Legal
lessons: Measure lag between resignation and Security notification
Decide whether departure-risk reviews should be automatic for named roles
Review privacy feedback on the proportionality of monitoring used

splunk.title: Departing user data movement summary
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false sum(Web.bytes_out) as upload from datamodel=Web where Web.user="<suspect_user>" Web.category IN ("online-storage*","personal-email*","web-based-email*") earliest=-30d by Web.dest _time span=1d

splunk.title: Personal email forwarding of attachments
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Email.file_name) as files from datamodel=Email where All_Email.src_user="<suspect_user>" All_Email.recipient IN ("*@gmail.com","*@outlook.com","*@yahoo.com","*@proton.me") earliest=-30d by All_Email.recipient

splunk.title: Access revocation verification after exit
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.user="<suspect_user>" Authentication.action=success earliest=<exit_date> by Authentication.app Authentication.src

playbooks.name: Disgruntled administrator sabotaging systems
playbooks.summary: Use when a privileged administrator in conflict with the organization deletes data, changes passwords, disables backups or alters configurations to cause damage.

preparation: Store break-glass admin credentials in a vault the administrators cannot change alone
Keep immutable or offline backups that admins cannot delete without dual approval
Forward admin audit logs to a SIEM tenant administered by a different team
identification: Confirm the scope of destructive actions: deleted VMs, dropped databases, disabled accounts, changed passwords
Attribute each action to the admin account, source host and time from audit logs
Check for backdoor accounts, new SSH keys or scheduled jobs created by the admin
Verify backup integrity and whether retention or snapshots were altered
Get HR context on the dispute, termination timing or grievances without sharing technical details widely
containment: Disable all the admin's accounts, including service and cloud console identities, in one coordinated action
Rotate shared admin, root and break-glass passwords the admin knew
Revoke the admin's VPN, SSH keys and hardware tokens
Coordinate with HR and Legal on removing the person from premises and whether to involve police
eradication: Remove backdoor accounts, cron jobs and authorized_keys entries the admin added
Revert configuration changes using version control or config backups
Audit firewall rules and DNS records for malicious edits
recovery: Restore deleted systems and data from immutable backups in business priority order
Validate restored systems with service owners before reopening to users
Preserve evidence with chain of custody for civil or criminal action
lessons: Introduce dual control for destructive operations on production and backups
Require HR to alert Security before adverse action against privileged staff
Review how many shared admin credentials existed and eliminate them

splunk.title: Destructive and account changes by the admin
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Changes.object) as objects from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.user="<suspect_admin>" All_Changes.action IN ("deleted","modified","disabled") by All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.command All_Changes.dest _time span=10m

splunk.title: Password resets and account disables in AD
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode IN (4724,4725,4726,4720,4728,4732) Subject_Account_Name="<suspect_admin>" | stats count values(Target_Account_Name) as targets by EventCode host

splunk.title: Backup job and snapshot deletions
splunk.spl: index=* (sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName IN ("DeleteSnapshot","DeleteBackupVault","DeleteRecoveryPoint","PutBackupVaultAccessPolicy")) OR (sourcetype="veeam:*" action IN ("delete*","retention*")) | stats count by user eventName

playbooks.name: Privileged user snooping on HR or medical records
playbooks.summary: Use when access audits show an employee viewing HR files, patient charts or customer accounts of colleagues, celebrities or relatives without a work reason.

preparation: Enable read-access auditing in the EHR, HRIS and customer support systems
Run proactive access monitoring for VIP, employee and same-surname record views
Agree a sanctions policy for inappropriate access with HR and the Privacy Officer
identification: Pull the access log for the user: records viewed, screens opened, timestamps and workstation
Check each viewed record against the user's assignments, tickets or care team to find unjustified views
Identify relationships between the user and the subjects such as same address, surname or manager chain
Determine whether data was printed, exported or screenshotted after viewing
Interview the user with HR present and record their explanation
containment: Restrict the user's role to the minimum needed for their current duties
Enable break-the-glass justification prompts for sensitive record access
Preserve the access logs and any exports under legal hold
eradication: Remove standing access to VIP and employee records from the user's role
Delete any exports or printouts recovered from the user
Remove shared or generic logins on clinical workstations that hid who viewed records
recovery: Provide the Privacy Officer the list of affected individuals for notification assessment
Prepare notification letters to affected individuals if required by the risk assessment
Apply HR sanctions according to the documented policy
lessons: Add automated alerts for employees viewing other employees' records
Review whether role-based access in the system is too broad
Track the number of inappropriate access cases per quarter

splunk.title: Records viewed by the user in the EHR
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="epic:access" OR sourcetype="ehr:audit" user="<suspect_user>" action IN ("view","print","export") | stats count values(action) as actions earliest(_time) as first by patient_id workstation | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Employees viewing records of other employees
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="ehr:audit" action=view | lookup employee_patients.csv patient_id OUTPUT employee_name | where isnotnull(employee_name) | stats count dc(patient_id) as records by user

splunk.title: HRIS sensitive page views
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="workday:audit" OR sourcetype="hris:audit" actor="<suspect_user>" task IN ("View Compensation","View Personal Data","View Medical Leave") | stats count by target_worker task

playbooks.name: Employee selling network access or credentials
playbooks.summary: Use when intel, a tip or anomalous logins suggest an employee is selling their VPN, SSO or admin access to outsiders, for example via forums or messaging channels.

preparation: Subscribe to intel monitoring for initial access listings that mention the company or its sector and size
Log VPN sessions with device posture, source IP and concurrent session counts
Keep a law enforcement liaison contact for insider criminal cases
identification: Correlate the listing details such as country, revenue band and access type with the company's footprint
Look for the employee's account logging in from hosting providers, new countries or unmanaged devices
Check for concurrent sessions where the employee is in the office while VPN sessions run elsewhere
Review recent MFA device registrations or resets on the account
Keep investigation confidential and limited to named investigators, HR and Legal
containment: Revoke all sessions and require MFA re-registration with identity verification
Block the external source IPs used by the buyer
Decide with Legal whether to monitor briefly for attribution or disable the account immediately
eradication: Hunt for persistence the buyer may have established: new accounts, implants, tunnels
Remove MFA methods registered by the outside party
Rotate credentials for any systems the buyer reached
recovery: Provide evidence packages to Legal for termination and possible referral to police
Re-validate that the access path is closed by testing with the old credential
Notify affected system owners of the access the buyer had
lessons: Add detection for concurrent sessions from geographically distant locations
Bind VPN access to managed devices with certificates
Review whether financial stress indicators are part of insider risk referral criteria

splunk.title: VPN sessions for the user by source and device
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="pan:globalprotect" OR sourcetype="cisco:asa" user="<suspect_user>" | iplocation src_ip | stats count earliest(_time) as first latest(_time) as last values(Country) as countries values(host_id) as devices by src_ip

splunk.title: Badge in office while remote session active
splunk.spl: index=* (sourcetype="badge:access" user="<suspect_user>") OR (sourcetype="pan:globalprotect" user="<suspect_user>" event_id="gateway-connected") | eval kind=if(sourcetype="badge:access","badge","vpn") | timechart span=15m count by kind

splunk.title: MFA method changes on the account
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("User registered security info","User deleted security info","Admin registered security info") targetResources{}.userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" | table _time activityDisplayName initiatedBy.user.ipAddress result

playbooks.name: Contractor accessing systems beyond their engagement scope
playbooks.summary: Use when a contractor or consultant account browses repositories, shares or systems not covered by their statement of work, or keeps access after the engagement ends.

preparation: Record each contractor's sponsor, scope and end date in the identity system
Expire contractor accounts automatically at the contract end date
Put contractors in a distinct group so their access can be monitored and reviewed
identification: Obtain the statement of work and sponsor's description of approved systems
List systems, repositories and shares the contractor accessed in the last 60 days
Flag access outside approved scope and check how permissions were granted
Check whether data was downloaded from out-of-scope locations
Notify the contractor's firm through Procurement and Legal per contract terms when appropriate
containment: Remove group memberships and permissions not required by the statement of work
Restrict the contractor to a jump host or VDI for remaining work
Preserve access logs for contractual dispute or claims
eradication: Recover or confirm deletion of any out-of-scope data with the contractor firm
Revoke personal access tokens and API keys issued to the contractor
Close inherited access from nested groups that caused the overreach
recovery: Confirm the sponsor re-approves the reduced access list
Schedule access recertification before any contract extension
Record the outcome with Procurement for vendor performance review
lessons: Measure how many contractor accounts exceed scope at quarterly reviews
Require sponsors to attest to contractor access every 90 days
Fix the provisioning template that granted broad default groups

splunk.title: Systems accessed by contractor accounts
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Authentication.dest) as systems values(Authentication.dest) as dests from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.user="<contractor_user>" Authentication.action=success earliest=-60d by Authentication.app

splunk.title: File share access outside approved paths
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5145 Account_Name="<contractor_user>" | stats count values(Relative_Target_Name) as files by Share_Name | lookup contractor_scope.csv share as Share_Name OUTPUT approved | where isnull(approved)

splunk.title: Contractor accounts active past end date
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false latest(_time) as last from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | lookup contractors.csv user as Authentication.user OUTPUT end_date | where isnotnull(end_date) AND last > strptime(end_date, "%Y-%m-%d")

playbooks.name: Fraud by a finance employee (payments or vendor records)
playbooks.summary: Use when a finance or accounts payable employee is suspected of creating fake vendors, changing bank details, or approving their own payments to divert funds.

preparation: Enable ERP audit trails for vendor master changes, bank detail edits and payment approvals
Enforce segregation of duties so no one can create a vendor and approve its payment
Agree with Internal Audit and Legal who leads fraud investigations and when Security assists
identification: Extract vendor master changes made by the employee, especially bank account and address edits
Match new vendor bank accounts against employee payroll bank accounts and addresses
List payments the employee created or approved and flag round amounts or split invoices below approval limits
Review email for invoice PDFs created by the employee rather than received from vendors
Keep the case restricted to Internal Audit, Legal, HR and named investigators
containment: Remove the employee's ERP vendor maintenance and payment approval roles
Place a hold on pending payments to the suspicious vendors
Ask Treasury to contact the bank about recalling recent transfers
eradication: Block the fraudulent vendor records in the ERP
Revert bank detail changes after verifying with vendors by known phone numbers
Image the employee's laptop and preserve mailbox under legal hold
recovery: Quantify the loss with Internal Audit for insurance and recovery claims
Notify the crime or fidelity insurer under policy conditions
Support Legal in any referral to law enforcement
lessons: Add a monthly match of vendor bank accounts against payroll accounts
Fix the SoD conflict in ERP roles that enabled the fraud
Require callback verification for all vendor bank detail changes

splunk.title: Vendor master changes by the employee
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="sap:audit" OR sourcetype="erp:audit" user="<suspect_user>" tcode IN ("XK01","XK02","FK02","FK01") | stats count values(field_changed) as fields values(vendor_id) as vendors by tcode

splunk.title: Payments created and approved by the same user
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="erp:payments" | where created_by=approved_by | stats count sum(amount) as total values(vendor_id) as vendors by created_by

splunk.title: Vendor bank accounts matching payroll
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="erp:vendor_master" | lookup payroll_bank_accounts.csv iban OUTPUT employee_id | where isnotnull(employee_id) | table vendor_id vendor_name iban employee_id

playbooks.name: Staff member running unauthorized cryptocurrency mining
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee uses company servers, GPUs, cloud accounts or workstations to mine cryptocurrency for personal gain.

preparation: Block known mining pool domains and Stratum ports at the proxy and firewall
Alert on sustained high GPU or CPU utilization on hosts without a declared workload
Set budget alerts on GPU instance families in cloud accounts
identification: Identify miner binaries (xmrig, ethminer, nbminer) and their command lines including wallet address
Record the mining pool host and port from network connections
Determine who deployed the miner from login records, cloud API calls or container registries
Calculate compute hours and cost consumed by the miner
Confirm with HR before interviewing the employee
containment: Kill the miner processes and stop or scale down mining instances
Block the mining pool domains and IPs
Remove the employee's ability to launch compute in the affected accounts
eradication: Delete miner binaries, containers, scheduled tasks and startup scripts
Remove the cloud instances, launch templates or Kubernetes deployments used for mining
Rotate any credentials the employee embedded in mining scripts
recovery: Return GPUs and servers to their legitimate workloads after a clean scan
Provide Finance the cost estimate for any recovery from the employee
Document outcome for HR disciplinary process
lessons: Add Stratum protocol detection on the IDS
Restrict GPU instance types with service control policies
Review why the utilization anomaly was not acted on sooner

splunk.title: Miner process execution
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("xmrig*","ethminer*","nbminer*","t-rex*","lolminer*") OR Processes.process="*stratum+tcp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user

splunk.title: Connections to mining pools
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count sum(All_Traffic.bytes) as bytes from datamodel=Network_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (3333,4444,5555,7777,14444,45700) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port

splunk.title: GPU instance launches in cloud
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName=RunInstances | spath requestParameters.instanceType output=itype | search itype IN ("p3*","p4*","g4*","g5*") | stats count by userIdentity.arn itype awsRegion

playbooks.name: Employee installed remote access software to work from elsewhere
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee installs AnyDesk, TeamViewer, Chrome Remote Desktop or similar on their work machine to reach it from home or abroad, bypassing VPN and location policy.

preparation: Maintain an allowlist of approved remote support tools and block others via application control
Detect remote access tool installs and outbound connections to their relay networks
Publish a remote and overseas working policy that states approved access methods
identification: Identify the tool, version, install time and installing user on the endpoint
Pull the tool's connection logs to find remote peer IDs and source IPs
Geolocate the remote sessions to check whether the employee was working from an unapproved country
Check whether any session originated from someone other than the employee
Review data accessed during remote sessions for export-control or data-residency concerns
containment: Uninstall the remote access tool and block its hash and relay domains
Terminate any active remote sessions
Reset the employee's password in case the tool stored unattended access credentials
eradication: Remove unattended-access services and startup entries the tool created
Hunt for the same tool on other endpoints
Confirm the employee has a supported VPN or VDI path for remote work
recovery: Return the endpoint to service after EDR scan
Have HR address the policy breach and any location-related tax or legal issues
Document whether any third party accessed the machine
lessons: Measure how many unapproved remote tools are discovered per quarter
Close local admin rights that allowed installation
Clarify the overseas working approval process to reduce workarounds

splunk.title: Remote access tools executed on endpoints
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count earliest(_time) as first from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","remoting_host.exe","rustdesk.exe","Splashtop*.exe","ScreenConnect*.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Connections to remote access relay networks
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query IN ("*.anydesk.com","*.teamviewer.com","remotedesktop-pa.googleapis.com","*.rustdesk.com") by DNS.src DNS.query

playbooks.name: Employees sharing account credentials
playbooks.summary: Use when evidence shows staff sharing passwords or MFA codes with colleagues, assistants or family members, breaking accountability and audit trails.

preparation: Provide delegated access features (mailbox delegation, shared mailboxes) so sharing is unnecessary
Log device fingerprint and source for every sign-in
State in the acceptable-use policy that credential sharing is prohibited
identification: Find concurrent sign-ins for the account from different devices or locations
Identify who else used the credential through device names, badge data or interviews
Check whether MFA push approvals came from a device owned by someone else
Determine whether the second person had their own account with lesser privileges
Assess what actions were performed under the shared identity
containment: Reset the password and revoke all sessions for the shared account
Re-register MFA on a device verified as owned by the account holder
Provision proper delegated access for the colleague who needed it
eradication: Remove the shared credential from notes, browser profiles or password managers of the other person
Delete MFA methods registered to devices not owned by the account holder
Convert any team-shared login into named accounts or a vaulted shared credential with checkout logging
recovery: Correct audit records where actions are attributed to the wrong person, with Legal guidance
Coach both employees with HR on policy and the reason for it
Confirm the account now signs in only from the owner's devices
lessons: Detect MFA approvals from devices registered to another user
Review why delegation was not used, such as missing training or tooling
Track repeat offenders for escalation

splunk.title: Concurrent sign-ins from different devices
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" status.errorCode=0 | bin _time span=15m | stats dc(deviceDetail.deviceId) as devices dc(ipAddress) as ips values(deviceDetail.displayName) as names by _time | where devices > 1

splunk.title: Okta sessions from multiple user agents
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType="user.session.start" actor.alternateId="<suspect_user>" outcome.result=SUCCESS | stats count values(client.userAgent.rawUserAgent) as ua values(client.ipAddress) as ips by client.device

playbooks.name: Employee approached or recruited by a ransomware group
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee reports, or intel reveals, that a ransomware affiliate offered them money to run malware or provide access, whether or not they accepted.

preparation: Publish a confidential channel and reassurance that staff who report approaches will be protected
Brief high-access roles such as IT admins and help desk on insider recruitment tactics
Have law enforcement cyber unit contacts ready
identification: Collect the approach messages, handles, platforms and any files or links sent, without interacting further
Determine whether the employee ran any provided file or shared credentials
Check the employee's endpoint for the provided payload hash or URLs
Review the employee's account for unusual logins since first contact
Assess whether other staff were approached by the same handles
containment: Block the payload hash, URLs and contact domains enterprise-wide
Reset the employee's credentials and MFA as a precaution
Increase monitoring on the employee's privileged systems for 30 days
eradication: Remove any payload or remote tool found on the endpoint
Hunt for the payload and indicators across all endpoints
Review and remove access the employee does not need, framed as protective not punitive
recovery: Report the approach to law enforcement with Legal's approval
Thank and support the reporting employee and document protection measures
If the employee cooperated with the group, hand over to HR and Legal with full evidence
lessons: Share sanitized indicators with industry ISAC peers
Add recruitment scenarios to insider awareness training
Measure time between approach and report

splunk.title: Execution of the payload offered to the employee
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count earliest(_time) as first from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_hash="<payload_hash>" OR Processes.process_name="<payload_name>" by Processes.dest Processes.user | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Access to contact or payload URLs across the org
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url IN ("*<ioc_domain>*") OR Web.dest="<ioc_ip>" by Web.user Web.src Web.url

splunk.title: New logins for the employee since first contact
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.user="<suspect_user>" earliest=<contact_date> by Authentication.src Authentication.dest Authentication.app | iplocation Authentication.src

playbooks.name: Logic bomb planted in code or scheduled jobs
playbooks.summary: Use when code review, a tip or a near-miss reveals time- or condition-triggered destructive code planted by an insider in applications, scripts, cron jobs or database triggers.

preparation: Require peer review and signed commits for production code and infrastructure scripts
Inventory scheduled jobs, cron entries and database triggers with an owner for each
Keep tested backups that predate recent changes by the departing or suspected insider
identification: Locate the trigger condition: date check, missing-user check or file-presence check in the code
Identify the commit, author, reviewer and deployment that introduced the code
Search all repositories, cron tables and DB triggers for similar patterns by the same author
Determine the trigger date or condition and how much time remains
Assess what the payload does: delete data, corrupt records, disable services
containment: Disable the scheduled job or trigger immediately without running it
Freeze deployments from the author's branches and revoke their repository write access
Take fresh backups of systems in the blast radius before changes
eradication: Remove the malicious code via reviewed commit and redeploy
Audit every commit by the author for the past year with a second reviewer
Rotate credentials the code or author had access to
recovery: Validate data integrity on systems if the bomb partially executed
Confirm the trigger date passes without impact under heightened monitoring
Hand forensic copies of commits and deployment logs to Legal
lessons: Add static analysis rules for date-conditional delete or drop statements
Enforce branch protection so no one merges unreviewed code to production
Review whether the reviewer of the commit missed it and why

splunk.title: Scheduled task and cron creation by the author
splunk.spl: index=* (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4698 Account_Name="<suspect_user>") OR (sourcetype="linux:audit" exe="/usr/bin/crontab" auid_name="<suspect_user>") | table _time host sourcetype Task_Name cmd

splunk.title: Commits and merges by the author to production branches
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="github:enterprise:audit" actor="<suspect_user>" action IN ("git.push","pull_request.merge","protected_branch.policy_override") | stats count values(repo) as repos by action

splunk.title: Mass delete operations near the trigger date
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.action=deleted by All_Changes.dest All_Changes.user _time span=5m | where count > 100

playbooks.name: Insider leaking confidential information to the press
playbooks.summary: Use when confidential internal documents or details appear in media reports and leadership asks for an investigation, balancing evidence gathering with whistleblower protections.

preparation: Have Legal define when a leak investigation is lawful given whistleblower and press protections
Use document watermarking or unique distribution versions for highly sensitive material
Keep access logs for board and executive document repositories
identification: Get Legal's written approval and scope before any investigative search begins
Identify exactly which document versions or details were published
List everyone who had access to that version from repository and distribution logs
Check access, download and print events for those documents in the window before publication
Assess whether the leak may be a protected disclosure and route to the whistleblower process if so
containment: Restrict access to the remaining sensitive documents in the same repository
Coordinate a communications response with PR and Legal
Avoid any contact with journalists outside the PR function
eradication: Remove broad distribution lists from the sensitive repository
Revoke external sharing links that exist on related documents
Apply sensitivity labels with encryption to the affected document set
recovery: Provide findings only to Legal and HR, stating confidence levels honestly
Ensure no retaliation occurs against a person whose disclosure is protected
Close the investigation formally with documented rationale
lessons: Review whether sensitive documents need per-recipient watermarking
Check that internal speak-up channels are trusted enough to be used before the press
Record investigative steps taken for proportionality review

splunk.title: Access to the leaked document before publication
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation IN ("FileAccessed","FileDownloaded","FilePrinted","FileCopied") ObjectId="*<document_name>*" earliest=<window_start> latest=<publication_time> | stats count values(Operation) as ops earliest(_time) as first by UserId ClientIP | convert ctime(first)

splunk.title: Sharing changes on the sensitive repository
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation IN ("SharingSet","AddedToGroup","AnonymousLinkCreated","SharingInvitationCreated") SiteUrl="*<site_path>*" | table _time UserId Operation ObjectId TargetUserOrGroupName

playbooks.name: Inappropriate access granted to friends or relatives
playbooks.summary: Use when an administrator or manager grants accounts, elevated roles or data access to relatives, friends or associates who lack a business need or proper approval.

preparation: Require ticket-linked approvals for account creation and privileged group changes
Collect conflict-of-interest declarations from staff with provisioning rights
Run quarterly access recertification by data owners
identification: List accounts and group memberships created or changed by the suspected administrator
Check each grant against an approved ticket and manager approval
Identify relationships between grantees and the administrator using HR data under Legal guidance
Review what the grantees accessed with the granted permissions
Check whether guest or contractor accounts were created without sponsors
containment: Suspend unapproved accounts and remove unapproved group memberships
Require a second approver for the administrator's future provisioning actions
Preserve provisioning logs and tickets
eradication: Delete orphan guest and contractor accounts tied to the grants
Correct role templates if the admin used a loophole to bypass approval
Revoke any API keys or tokens issued to the grantees
recovery: Restore proper access for any grantee with a genuine, approved business need
Report findings to HR and Compliance for conflict-of-interest handling
Confirm data accessed by grantees for any privacy impact
lessons: Add a detection for account creation without a matching ticket ID
Enforce four-eyes approval on privileged group membership changes
Review effectiveness of conflict-of-interest declarations

splunk.title: Accounts created and groups changed by the admin
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode IN (4720,4728,4732,4756) Subject_Account_Name="<suspect_admin>" | stats count values(Group_Name) as groups by Target_Account_Name EventCode

splunk.title: Entra ID guest invitations by the admin
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("Invite external user","Add user","Add member to role") initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName="<suspect_admin>" | table _time activityDisplayName targetResources{}.userPrincipalName result

splunk.title: Provisioning actions without a ticket reference
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.object_category=user All_Changes.action=created by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object _time | lookup provisioning_tickets.csv account as All_Changes.object OUTPUT ticket | where isnull(ticket)

playbooks.name: Employee secretly surveilling colleagues
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee, often IT staff or a manager, uses admin tools, mailbox access, keyloggers or cameras to monitor coworkers without authorization.

preparation: Log mailbox delegation grants, FullAccess permissions and MailItemsAccessed events
Require Legal and HR authorization for any sanctioned employee monitoring
Detect keylogger and screen-capture tools on endpoints
identification: Identify which mailboxes, chats, cameras or devices the employee accessed and how
Check for FullAccess or delegate permissions the employee granted to themselves
Look for keylogger or monitoring agents installed on colleagues' devices
Confirm there was no authorized investigation that covers the activity
Identify affected colleagues while keeping their identities restricted
containment: Remove the employee's mailbox permissions and admin roles used for surveillance
Uninstall monitoring agents from affected devices after evidence capture
Disable camera or DVR accounts the employee used
eradication: Delete collected recordings and logs the employee held, after Legal preserves evidence
Remove eDiscovery or content search roles not tied to approved cases
Rotate passwords for colleagues whose credentials may have been keylogged
recovery: Inform affected colleagues with HR and Legal guidance and offer support
Assess whether the surveillance is a reportable personal data breach
Apply HR disciplinary action per policy
lessons: Alert on self-granted mailbox permissions by administrators
Separate eDiscovery rights from general IT admin roles
Review physical security camera access controls

splunk.title: Mailbox permissions granted by the employee
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation IN ("Add-MailboxPermission","Add-MailboxFolderPermission","Set-Mailbox") UserId="<suspect_user>" | spath Parameters{} | table _time Operation ObjectId Parameters{}.Name Parameters{}.Value

splunk.title: Mail items accessed in others' mailboxes
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="o365:management:activity" Operation=MailItemsAccessed UserId="<suspect_user>" | where MailboxOwnerUPN!=UserId | stats count by MailboxOwnerUPN ClientIPAddress

splunk.title: Keylogging and monitoring agents on endpoints
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("*keylog*","refog*","spyrix*","kidlogger*","ActivTrak*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name

playbooks.name: Personal use of company systems creating legal risk
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee uses company devices or networks for activity that exposes the organization legally, such as pirated content distribution, harassment, or running a side business.

preparation: Publish an acceptable-use policy that employees acknowledge annually
Define with Legal when illegal content must go to law enforcement rather than internal handling
Keep proxy and DLP logs with user attribution
identification: Classify the activity: copyright infringement notice, harassment, outside business, or potentially illegal content
Collect the triggering evidence such as a DMCA notice, complaint or proxy log
Map activity to the user via DHCP, VPN and proxy authentication records
Stop and escalate to Legal without viewing further if content may be illegal imagery
Limit evidence handling to the minimum people Legal approves
containment: Block the peer-to-peer or offending service for the user or network segment
Isolate the device and preserve it unaltered if law enforcement referral is likely
Respond to any third-party notice via Legal only
eradication: Remove torrent clients or unapproved software from the device
Delete pirated content from company storage after Legal confirms preservation needs
Revoke access used for outside business activity
recovery: Hand findings to HR for disciplinary handling
Answer the copyright holder or complainant through Legal
Return the device to service after reimaging
lessons: Add peer-to-peer protocol blocking on guest and corporate networks
Review whether acceptable-use training reached the employee's group
Track volume of copyright notices received by network segment

splunk.title: Peer-to-peer traffic by user
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="pan:traffic" app IN ("bittorrent","emule","gnutella") | stats sum(bytes) as bytes earliest(_time) as first latest(_time) as last by src_user src_ip | convert ctime(first) ctime(last)

splunk.title: Map IP and time from a third-party notice to a user
splunk.spl: index=* (sourcetype="pan:traffic" OR sourcetype="dhcp") (src_ip="<nat_internal_ip>" OR nat_src_ip="<public_ip>") earliest=<notice_time_minus_1h> latest=<notice_time_plus_1h> | stats values(src_user) as users values(src_ip) as internal values(dest_port) as ports by nat_src_port

playbooks.name: Fraudulent remote IT worker hired under a false identity
playbooks.summary: Use when a remote hire shows signs of being a sanctioned-state or fraudulent worker: laptop farms, mismatched identity, remote-control tools, or pay routed to unusual accounts.

preparation: Require live video identity verification and document checks for remote technical hires
Ship laptops only to verified home addresses and flag reshipping or freight-forwarder addresses
Detect IP-KVM devices and remote control tools on corporate laptops
identification: Compare the laptop's sign-in IPs against the worker's stated location and flag VPN or VPS exits
Check the endpoint for IP-KVM USB devices, AnyDesk, Chrome Remote Desktop or similar tooling
Review the hiring file for identity inconsistencies: reused photos, mismatched documents, references
Check payroll for bank changes, payment platforms or accounts in third countries
Review code commits and data access for exfiltration or unusual scope
containment: Disable the worker's accounts and revoke all tokens in one coordinated action
Remotely lock the laptop and request return via a verified courier
Freeze pending payroll payments with Finance and Legal input
eradication: Audit code and infrastructure changes made by the worker and revert suspicious ones
Rotate secrets and keys the worker could access in repos and CI
Search for other hires sharing the same addresses, bank accounts, phone numbers or devices
recovery: Have Legal assess sanctions exposure and reporting to relevant authorities
Report the case to the FBI or national cyber authority as advised by counsel
Restore any affected systems and confirm no remaining persistence
lessons: Add continuous checks for sign-ins from known VPS and residential proxy ranges for new hires
Strengthen identity proofing in recruitment with HR and Talent Acquisition
Share indicators with industry peers through the ISAC

splunk.title: Sign-in sources for the worker
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" | iplocation ipAddress | stats count values(City) as cities values(Country) as countries values(autonomousSystemNumber) as asn by ipAddress

splunk.title: Remote control tools and IP-KVM devices on the laptop
splunk.spl: index=* host="<host>" ((sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image IN ("*AnyDesk*","*remoting_host*","*TeamViewer*","*rustdesk*")) OR (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=6416 Device_Description IN ("*KVM*","*PiKVM*","*TinyPilot*"))) | stats count values(Image) as image values(Device_Description) as device by host

splunk.title: Other users sharing the worker's IPs
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false dc(Authentication.user) as users values(Authentication.user) as accounts from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.src IN ("<ioc_ip1>","<ioc_ip2>") by Authentication.src

playbooks.name: Intern or junior hire with excessive access
playbooks.summary: Use when an intern, apprentice or new junior employee is found with admin rights, production access or sensitive data access far beyond their role, whether or not misuse has occurred.

preparation: Use role-based onboarding templates for interns with no privileged groups by default
Expire intern accounts at the internship end date
Include intern accounts in monthly privileged access reports
identification: List the intern's group memberships, roles and data access and compare with the role template
Find how the excess access was granted: cloned account, manager request or inherited group
Review what the intern did with privileged rights in the last 30 days
Check whether sensitive data was downloaded or shared
Speak with the manager about the work the intern actually needs to do
containment: Remove privileged groups and production roles not required
Move the intern's needed access to a supervised or time-bound grant
Review and remove any credentials the intern created with privileged rights
eradication: Fix the source account or template that was cloned with excess rights
Remove other new hires who received the same cloned access
Delete service accounts or keys created by the intern if unapproved
recovery: Confirm the intern can still complete assigned work with reduced access
Record that no misuse occurred, or escalate to HR if misuse is found
Notify data owners if sensitive data was viewed unnecessarily
lessons: Stop account cloning as a provisioning method
Alert when new accounts under 30 days old join privileged groups
Measure how many accounts exceed their role template at each review

splunk.title: Privileged group membership for new accounts
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode IN (4728,4732,4756) Group_Name IN ("Domain Admins","Enterprise Admins","Administrators","*Prod*") Member_Name="*<intern_user>*" | table _time Subject_Account_Name Group_Name Member_Name

splunk.title: Privileged actions by the intern
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Change where All_Changes.user="<intern_user>" by All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action All_Changes.dest

splunk.title: Cloud admin role assignments to recent accounts
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName="Add member to role" | spath targetResources{}.modifiedProperties{}.newValue output=role | search role="*Admin*" | table _time targetResources{}.userPrincipalName role initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName

playbooks.name: Terminated employee still has working access
playbooks.summary: Use when a former employee's account, VPN, SaaS login, API key or shared credential is still active after termination, or logs show them using it.

preparation: Drive deprovisioning from the HRIS termination event through SCIM to all SSO-connected apps
Maintain an inventory of non-SSO apps and shared credentials needing manual offboarding
Give Security a same-day termination feed for involuntary exits
identification: List all identities the former employee held: AD, SSO, SaaS local accounts, cloud keys, SSH keys
Search authentication logs for any use of those identities after the termination date
Identify actions taken post-termination such as downloads, deletes or config changes
Determine whether shared or team passwords known to the person were rotated
Check whether the former employee's MFA device is still registered
containment: Disable every remaining identity and revoke sessions and tokens
Rotate shared passwords and API keys the person knew
Block the source IPs used after termination if access was attempted
eradication: Delete SSH keys and personal access tokens tied to the person in Git, cloud and servers
Remove the person from vendor portals and external admin consoles
Transfer ownership of files, repos and resources to the manager
recovery: Undo any post-termination changes and restore deleted data
Ask Legal to send a cease-access letter if deliberate use occurred
Verify with a test login that each identity is disabled
lessons: Measure time from termination to full deprovisioning across all systems
Connect the remaining non-SSO apps to SCIM or SSO
Add an alert for any successful login by a terminated user

splunk.title: Logins by the user after termination
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count earliest(_time) as first latest(_time) as last from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.user="<former_user>" Authentication.action=success earliest=<termination_date> by Authentication.app Authentication.src Authentication.dest | convert ctime(first) ctime(last)

splunk.title: AWS access keys used after termination
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" userIdentity.userName="<former_user>" earliest=<termination_date> | stats count values(eventName) as actions values(sourceIPAddress) as ips by userIdentity.accessKeyId

splunk.title: Successful logins by terminated users
splunk.spl: | tstats summariesonly=false count latest(_time) as last from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user | lookup terminated_users.csv user as Authentication.user OUTPUT term_date | where isnotnull(term_date) AND last > strptime(term_date, "%Y-%m-%d")

playbooks.name: Insider approving MFA or resetting accounts for an external attacker
playbooks.summary: Use when an employee or help desk agent knowingly approves MFA prompts, resets MFA or grants access for an outside attacker, often after being paid or coerced.

preparation: Require identity verification steps logged in the ticket for every help desk MFA reset
Enable number matching and location context in MFA prompts
Log help desk reset actions with the agent, target and ticket ID
identification: Find MFA approvals or resets followed by sign-ins from attacker-linked IPs
Check whether the approving employee's actions match social engineering or deliberate collusion patterns
Review the help desk agent's reset volume and verification evidence for each ticket
Identify all accounts the agent reset in the period and their subsequent sign-ins
Engage HR and Legal before interviewing the suspected insider
containment: Revoke sessions and re-secure every account the insider helped compromise
Remove the agent's reset and admin privileges
Block attacker IPs and device IDs seen after the resets
eradication: Remove MFA methods registered by the attacker
Hunt for persistence the attacker created after gaining access: app consents, forwarding rules, new users
Rotate credentials for privileged accounts the attacker reached
recovery: Re-enroll affected users' MFA with in-person or video verification
Preserve evidence for criminal referral if collusion is confirmed
Restore help desk reset rights through a dual-approval workflow
lessons: Require a second approver for MFA resets on privileged accounts
Alert when one agent performs resets followed by risky sign-ins
Review insider risk indicators that were missed before the event

splunk.title: MFA resets by help desk agent and follow-on sign-ins
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType IN ("user.mfa.factor.reset_all","user.mfa.factor.deactivate","user.account.reset_password") actor.alternateId="<agent>" | stats count values(target{}.alternateId) as targets by actor.alternateId

splunk.title: MFA push approvals followed by new-location sign-in
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userPrincipalName="<target_user>" authenticationDetails{}.authenticationMethod="Mobile app notification" status.errorCode=0 | iplocation ipAddress | table _time ipAddress Country appDisplayName deviceDetail.displayName

splunk.title: Attacker-registered MFA methods
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("User registered security info","Admin registered security info") earliest=<reset_time> | table _time targetResources{}.userPrincipalName initiatedBy.user.ipAddress additionalDetails{}.value

playbooks.name: Whistleblower report alleging security misconduct
playbooks.summary: Use when a whistleblower or ethics hotline report alleges security misconduct such as concealed breaches or falsified audits, and the IR team must investigate while protecting the reporter.

preparation: Route ethics hotline reports about security to a named investigator independent of the accused team
Document whistleblower protection obligations with Legal for each jurisdiction
Keep a restricted case system where reporter identity is masked
identification: Record the allegation exactly as received and acknowledge receipt to the reporter via the hotline
Confirm the investigator has no conflict of interest with the accused
Identify systems, tickets and logs that can verify or refute the allegation
Collect evidence without alerting the accused team, using read-only access
Assess whether the allegation describes an unreported breach requiring notification
containment: Protect the reporter's identity in all communications and access lists
Preserve relevant logs, tickets and emails under legal hold before evidence can be altered
Escalate to the audit committee if senior leadership is implicated
eradication: Correct any falsified audit evidence or control attestations found
Remove the accused's ability to alter relevant records during the investigation
Fix the underlying control failure the report exposed
recovery: Trigger breach notification workflows if a concealed incident is confirmed
Give the reporter feedback within the timeframe required by policy or law
Monitor for any retaliation against the reporter and report it to Legal
lessons: Review why the issue was raised through the hotline rather than normal escalation
Measure time to acknowledge and to conclude whistleblower cases
Assess the independence of the security investigation function

splunk.title: Changes to incident or audit records by the accused
splunk.spl: index=* sourcetype="snow:incident" OR sourcetype="snow:sys_audit" user="<accused_user>" | stats count values(fieldname) as fields values(documentkey) as records by tablename

splunk.title: Log deletion or retention changes in the window
splunk.spl: index=* (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=1102) OR (sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName IN ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail","PutBucketLifecycle")) OR (index=_audit action=delete_by_keyword) | table _time host user eventName EventCode
